tasks.gr11-ml-patterns-t1: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy Term 1 — Patterns, Relationships and Representations. Ask learners to interpret values from tables and graphs, identify increasing or decreasing trends, compare two options represented in different ways (table vs graph vs formula), select the most useful representation for a given situation, and describe relationships in plain language. Use realistic contexts such as cell phone data costs, electricity usage, or petrol consumption graphs.
tasks.gr11-ml-conversions-time-t1: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy Term 1 — Measurement: Conversions and Time. Ask learners to convert between metric units of length (mm, cm, m, km), mass (mg, g, kg, t) and capacity (ml, l, kl), perform compound conversions (e.g. km/h to m/s), calculate elapsed time from timetables and schedules, and solve multi-step time problems involving 12-hour and 24-hour notation. Use contexts such as bus schedules, cooking, travel times and sports events.
tasks.gr11-ml-finance-docs-t1: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy Term 1 — Finance: Documents and Tariffs. Ask learners to read and interpret financial documents including payslips, invoices, receipts and bank statements; calculate VAT (15%) on items; understand tariff structures (fixed charge plus per-unit rate); compare two-part tariffs for electricity or water; and identify income, gross pay, deductions and net pay on a payslip. Use realistic South African contexts.
tasks.gr11-ml-break-even-t1: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy Term 1 — Finance: Budgets and Break-even. Ask learners to construct and interpret income-and-expenditure statements, calculate cost price, selling price and markup (as rand value and percentage), determine profit or loss, identify the break-even point on a graph or by calculation, and make justified decisions about pricing or budget options. Use small business or school fundraiser contexts relevant to South African learners.
